steps.body: Knowing WHY a strategy works matters as much as using it. Each strategy works because it protects the total while making the counting easier.
steps.narration: Knowing WHY a strategy works matters as much as using it. Each strategy works because it protects the total while making the counting easier.

widget.prompt: Explain-by-checking: the claim is that 3 + 9 equals 9 + 3. Start at 9 and count on 3. Where do you land?
widget.missFeedback: Start at 9 and count on 3: you land on 12.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 12 — the swapped order reaches the same total, which is the whole reason swapping is safe.

predict.prompt: A strategy changes HOW you count. What must it never change?

options.label: The total
The order of the numbers

predict.reveal: A strategy is only valid if the total survives it — the counting path may change freely.

misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g1p explain.

explanationVariants: A valid strategy protects the total.
The explanation names what stays the same.

options.label: Both orders join the same two groups
options.feedback: Correct — 4 + 9 and 9 + 4 combine the same counters, so the total 13 cannot change.

options.label: The bigger number always wins
options.feedback: Addition has no winner; both addends contribute fully to the total.

options.label: Swapping adds one extra
options.feedback: Swapping moves no counter in or out of the pile, so nothing extra can appear in the total.

options.label: It only works for small numbers
options.feedback: The two groups are the same two groups at any size, so the rule holds for all numbers.

explanationVariants: Make-ten regroups counters without changing the pile.
Explaining the move shows why it is safe.

widget.prompt: Why does making ten help with 8 + 6?

options.label: Ten and some more is easy to name
options.feedback: Correct — moving part of 6 to complete ten turns the sum into ten-and-leftovers, which is easy to read.

options.label: It changes the total to a rounder number
options.feedback: Making ten regroups the counters without changing the total at all.

options.label: Ten is bigger than both addends
options.feedback: The size of ten is not the point; its usefulness is that ten-and-more is easy to name.

options.label: It skips adding the leftover
options.feedback: The leftover must still be added; the strategy only reorders the work.
